steps.title: Potentiometer -> LED Brightness

quickCheck.question: What numeric range does analogWrite() accept on an Arduino Uno PWM pin?
quickCheck.explanation: `analogWrite()` modulates PWM duty cycle using an 8-bit value from 0 (0% duty cycle) to 255 (100% duty cycle).
quickCheck.warmupExplanation: PWM outputs in Arduino use 8-bit resolution, which spans from 0 to 255.

quickCheck.question: Why must you divide analogRead() by 4 or use map() before sending the value to analogWrite()?
options: Because analogRead is 10-bit (0-1023) while analogWrite only takes 8-bit (0-255)
Because the potentiometer will overheat otherwise
quickCheck.explanation: Passing values greater than 255 into `analogWrite()` causes register overflow and erratic brightness jumps.
quickCheck.warmupExplanation: 10-bit input (0-1023) is 4 times larger than 8-bit output (0-255), requiring scaling.

steps.title: Mapping 10-Bit Input to 8-Bit Output
steps.markdownContent:
The map() Function
int brightness = map(sensorVal, 0, 1023, 0, 255); scales the analog input range down to PWM range!

questions.question: Why must an analogRead value (0-1023) be scaled down before passing to analogWrite (0-255)?
questions.explanation: analogWrite only accepts 0-255. Dividing by 4 or using map() scales the ranges correctly!

questions.question: What convenient Arduino function rescales a number from one range to another?
questions.explanation: The built-in map() function calculates proportional scaling between any two numerical ranges!
